explanations: terra: Whatever good people advance for themselves they will find with Allah, so the surrendered possession is preserved as a future divine return.

luna: This account of righteousness includes giving wealth despite love for it (“عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ”) and belief in the Last Day. It joins the section’s material gift to faith in the promised end. | terra: This definition of righteousness joins belief in the Last Day, giving beloved wealth, and keeping covenants before concluding أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا; enacted giving displays truth.
terra: A person sells himself seeking God's satisfaction, expanding the section's surrendered wealth into the surrender of the self for رضا.

luna: The “good loan” to God is multiplied, and the ayah ends by saying to Him is the return. This ties parting with wealth to the final reckoning that grounds the section’s promise. | terra: The invitation to lend Allah a good loan promises manifold multiplication and places constriction, abundance, and return in God's hands.

luna: Believers are told to spend from God’s provision before a Day with no trade or friendship. It makes the section’s “give now for the end” concrete and removes human exchange as a way to secure that end. | terra: Believers are commanded to spend from God's provision before a day arrives with no trade, friendship, or intercession; giving today answers a specifically announced end.
luna: The parable is explicitly about spending in God’s way: one seed yields many times its amount. It makes the section’s present gift for a future return concrete as multiplied reward.

luna: Those who spend and do not follow it with reminders or injury have their reward with their Lord. This gives a specific form to giving without seeking repayment from the recipient. | terra: Those who spend without following expenditure by reminders or injury have their reward with their Lord, with neither fear nor grief.
terra: Charity spoiled by reminders, injury, and display becomes barren and earns nothing, marking the boundary around the section's giver who seeks only his Lord's face.

luna: The spenders here seek God’s approval (“ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ”) and firm their own souls; the garden parable ties that motive to a secure result, like the section’s gift seeking the Lord’s face. | terra: Those who spend seeking مَرْضَاتِ اللَّهِ and inner certainty are likened to a fruitful elevated garden; the giving itself seeks divine satisfaction and confirms its return.
terra: In the setting of spending, Satan promises poverty while Allah promises forgiveness and bounty; the giver's act reveals which opposed promise governs him.

luna: This ayah links spending to “ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ” and says what is spent is paid back in full. It clarifies how the giver can seek God alone without expecting payment from a recipient. | terra: Proper spending is only ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ اللَّهِ, and whatever good is spent is repaid in full; it joins the section's exclusive motive to assured recompense.

luna: Those who spend their wealth openly and secretly have their reward with their Lord (“فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ”). Their giving and assured recompense parallel the section’s giver and final outcome.
luna: This ayah says people will return to God and each soul will be paid in full for what it earned. It places the section’s root ج ز ي and second-life recompense at the return to God.
terra: Worldly desires and wealth are temporary enjoyment, while وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الْمَآبِ; the good return with God prepares 3:15's better promise.
terra: Against immediate desires, the God-fearing are promised Gardens, purified spouses, and رِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ; divine satisfaction is the better thing kept with God.

luna: The verse says righteousness is not reached until one spends what one loves (“مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ”). It clarifies the cost of the section’s gift of wealth as a confirming act. | terra: People do not attain al-birr until they spend from what they love; the desired good is reached through the concrete surrender of what is presently held.
luna: The righteous spend in ease and hardship (“يُنفِقُونَ فِى ٱلسَّرَّآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ”). This supplies a concrete giving practice among those promised the Garden; 3:136 names their reward.
luna: The reward of the people described in 3:134 is forgiveness and Gardens. It completes the connection between their spending and the section’s promised final good.
terra: Allah had made His promise true when the believers struck their enemy by His leave; their later faltering marks how conduct affects the experience of an already truthful promise.
terra: The follower of God's رضوان cannot be equated with one who returns under wrath to Hell, making divine satisfaction the boundary between opposed final destinations.

luna: Those who withhold God’s bounty learn that what they withheld will be put around their necks (“سَيُطَوَّقُونَ مَا بَخِلُوا۟ بِهِۦ”). It reverses the section’s giving and shows stored wealth becoming a judgment, not security. | terra: Those who withhold what Allah gave must not reckon withholding good for them: what they hoarded will encircle them on the Last Day, while the inheritance of all belongs to Allah.

luna: Every soul is paid its reward in full on Resurrection Day; success is entering the Garden and failure is the deluded life of this world. This directly joins the section’s last-life recompense to opposed outcomes.
luna: God does not wrong even an atom’s weight and multiplies good deeds, giving a great reward. It illustrates the section’s account of compensation as a real return that can exceed the deed.

luna: This verse explicitly says that those striving with wealth and lives are not like those who stay behind, then says “وَكُلًّا وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ.” It joins giving, al-husnā, and the promise in one formulation. | terra: Those who strive with wealth and life exceed those who sit, although وَكُلًّا وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنَىٰ; it directly relates enacted sacrifice, promise, and al-husna.
luna: This neighbor expands the promised good in 4:95 into degrees, forgiveness, and mercy. It adds the form of reward attached to the same striving with wealth and lives.
terra: Charity and other good action done seeking God's satisfaction receive a great reward, joining giving, divine رضا, and promised recompense.

luna: Believers who do good are promised Gardens, and the ayah calls this God’s true promise (“وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقًّۭا”). It names the assurance the section says the giver confirms by action. | terra: After promising believers Gardens, Allah calls His promise true and asks وَمَنْ أَصْدَقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ قِيلًا, answering the implicit charge against the promiser's truthfulness.

luna: This says outcomes are not by wish: whoever does evil is recompensed for it, while the believing doer of good enters the Garden. It directly ties the section’s opposed belief and action to opposite ends.
terra: Whoever seeks worldly reward is told that with Allah are both the reward of this world and of the hereafter, combining the two domains under the one giver of recompense.
terra: On the Day truthfulness benefits the truthful, Gardens are their reward, and رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ completes it with mutual satisfaction.
terra: The statement that the opponents do not يُكَذِّبُونَكَ but repudiate Allah's signs illuminates the section's dictionary point that takdhīb attaches a speaker or message to falsehood.

luna: The section’s root ج ز ي names recompense that can go either way; here a good deed is multiplied, while an evil deed receives only its like (“فَلَا يُجْزَىٰٓ إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا”). | terra: A good deed receives tenfold return while an evil deed is requited only with its like, displaying jazāʾ's two directions and the generosity of the good side.
terra: The people of the Garden say they found their Lord's promise true and ask the people of the Fire whether they found theirs true; both directions of the promised end have become experience.
terra: The believers are given glad tidings of mercy, satisfaction from Allah, and enduring Gardens, placing abundant رضا within the announced good end.
luna: This ayah condemns hoarding gold and silver without spending it in God’s way (“يَكْنِزُونَ ٱلذَّهَبَ وَٱلْفِضَّةَ”); it names the opposite use of wealth to the section’s giver.
luna: This neighbor gives the consequence of 9:34’s hoarding: the stored metal is heated and used to brand its owners. It makes withholding end in punishment rather than the section’s satisfaction.
terra: أَرَضِيتُمْ بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا مِنَ الْآخِرَةِ rebukes satisfaction with the near life in place of the hereafter, a misplaced رضا opposite the section's final satisfaction.
terra: إِحْدَى الْحُسْنَيَيْنِ names either victory or martyrdom as one of “the two best outcomes”; unlike the section's Garden sense, al-husna here embraces two hoped-for outcomes.
terra: After promising Gardens and good dwellings, the ayah declares رِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ; the abundant satisfaction named by the section exceeds even the pictured reward.
terra: Some believers treat what they spend as means of nearness to Allah and the Messenger's prayers, and Allah promises to admit them into His mercy.
terra: The foremost believers and their good followers receive mutual satisfaction—رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ—together with prepared Gardens.

luna: God has bought the believers’ lives and wealth in exchange for the Garden (“بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلْجَنَّةَ”) and calls it a true promise. This is a direct promise-and-gift formulation of the section’s image. | terra: Allah purchases believers' lives and wealth in exchange for the Garden, calls it a binding promise, and asks who is more faithful to covenant; present surrender trusts the promised return.
terra: Every small or large expenditure is recorded so that Allah may reward them by the best of what they did, directly linking spending to best final recompense.

luna: This ayah says God begins creation and repeats it so He can recompense believers who do good, and calls His promise true. It joins the section’s second creation and promised reward in one claim.
terra: Immediately before al-husna in 10:26, Allah calls to the Abode of Peace and guides to a straight path; it establishes al-husna as the destination of a divine invitation.

luna: The section’s named root ح س ن glosses al-husnā as Paradise; 10:26 gives good-doers al-husnā with an increase and immediately names the Garden, while their faces escape gloom and humiliation. | terra: This is the verse behind the section's definition: those who do good receive الْحُسْنَىٰ and an increase, with faces free of gloom and humiliation.

luna: This neighbor supplies the opposite of 10:26’s al-husnā: evil-doers are recompensed for evil and covered by humiliation. Its faces and outcome give the section’s best-versus-bad contrast a concrete form. | terra: The next ayah supplies al-husna's other face: evil earners receive a matching requital and their faces are covered by abasement and pieces of dark night.
terra: Those who want worldly life and its adornment are paid their works in it without reduction, showing a return confined to the first life.
terra: Those seekers have only the Fire in the hereafter and their works there collapse, the adverse final side of choosing the present payment in 11:15.

luna: This verse joins patience, spending from God’s provision, and seeking the Lord’s face (“ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِمْ”); it then promises the final home, closely matching gift, motive, and end in the section. | terra: Those seeking their Lord's face spend secretly and openly and repel evil with good; their action leads to عُقْبَى الدَّارِ, the good final home.
luna: This neighbor identifies the final home promised in 13:22 as Gardens of Eden (“جَنَّـٰتُ عَدْنٍۢ”). It supplies the garden detail behind the section’s al-husnā as Paradise.
luna: For those who believe and do good, this ayah promises “طُوبَىٰ لَهُمْ وَحُسْنُ مَـَٔابٍۢ,” blessedness and a good return. It directly states the good final outcome behind al-husnā.

luna: Believers are told to spend from what God provided before a Day without trade or friendship. Like 2:254, it ties present giving to a future in which people cannot settle accounts with one another. | terra: Believing servants are told to spend secretly and openly before a day comes with neither trade nor friendship, making present generosity the response to a known deadline.

luna: The verse says good-doers have good in this world and that the home of the Hereafter is better (“وَلَدَارُ ٱلْأَخِرَةِ خَيْرٌۭ”), linking good action to the superior final abode. | terra: Those who say their Lord sent good are told that good-doers have good here and that the home of the hereafter is better, joining received truth, conduct, and the best home.
terra: Everlasting Gardens are the destination of the God-fearing and contain what they desire, making concrete the better final home announced in 16:30.

terra: People ascribe to Allah what they hate while their tongues falsely claim أَنَّ لَهُمُ الْحُسْنَىٰ; their assigned end is the Fire, matching the section's portrait of treating the best outcome as an entitlement.
terra: What people possess runs out while what is with Allah remains, and He will reward the steadfast by the best of their deeds; this states why one can give the present away for the final end.

luna: For a believing man or woman who does right, God promises a good life and recompense according to “بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ.” The best-measure formula echoes the section’s promised outcome.
terra: Whoever desires the immediate life receives only what Allah wills and then is assigned Hell; it is the opposite orientation to striving for the hereafter in 17:19.

luna: The one who desires the Hereafter, strives for it as it deserves, and believes has effort appreciated (“مَّشْكُورًۭا”). It connects present action and belief to an accepted future end. | terra: Whoever desires the hereafter and strives for it with its proper striving has that striving appreciated; present action is directed toward and validated by the final end.
terra: Allah extends His giving to both the seekers of the immediate and the seekers of the hereafter, so every present gift remains a grant from the Lord.
terra: Worldly differences in divine favor are followed by the statement that the hereafter has greater ranks and distinction, locating the decisive superiority at the end.
terra: The prosperous garden-owner enters while wronging himself and assumes his present garden will never perish, grounding his false confidence in what he currently holds.
terra: He doubts the Hour yet claims that, even if returned to his Lord, he will find a better resort; this closely parallels 41:50's unsupported claim to al-husna.

luna: Worldly wealth and children are adornment, while lasting good deeds are better with the Lord for reward and hope (“وَٱلْبَـٰقِيَـٰتُ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتُ خَيْرٌ”). It explains why giving wealth for the end outranks holding it. | terra: Wealth and children are adornment of the worldly life, while lasting good deeds are better with the Lord in reward and hope; present holdings are weighed against enduring return.

luna: Dhul-Qarnayn’s other outcome is punishment for the one who wrongs (“فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُۥ”). Verse 18:88 supplies the believer’s al-husnā, completing the same two-way judgment as the section. | terra: Dhul-Qarnayn first assigns punishment to the wrongdoer and a harsher return to his Lord; it is the punitive direction of jazāʾ beside 18:88's beautiful recompense.

luna: The section explicitly pairs al-husnā with recompense and ease; this verse gives the believer “جَزَآءً ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ” and an easy word. Its contrast with 18:87 completes Dhul-Qarnayn’s two outcomes. | terra: Dhul-Qarnayn joins faith and right action to جَزَاءً الْحُسْنَىٰ and to an easy command, bringing the section's best outcome, recompense, and ease into one verdict.
terra: Ishmael is called صَادِقَ الْوَعْدِ, a human-side use of the root in which fidelity is shown by fulfilling what one has promised.
terra: The Hour is coming so that every soul may be requited for what it strives; this directly joins the second creation, diverse striving, and final jazāʾ.

terra: Moses asks whether his people were not given a good promise by their Lord and whether they broke their appointment because the wait seemed long; present conduct either holds to or betrays a promised good.
terra: ثُمَّ صَدَقْنَاهُمُ الْوَعْدَ describes Allah making the promise to His messengers come true through rescue and the destruction of excess-doers.
terra: Those for whom الْحُسْنَىٰ has already gone forth from Allah are kept far from Hell, explicitly making al-husna a prior divine determination of the good end.
terra: The angels meet those spared from Hell with the announcement that this is the day they were promised; it completes 21:101's prior al-husna as a promise now encountered.

luna: Those who migrate for God and are killed or die are promised good provision (“رِزْقًا حَسَنًۭا”). Their loss in God’s cause followed by divine provision parallels giving up what one has for the good end.
luna: God promises to admit them to an entry “يَرْضَوْنَهُۥ,” one that pleases them. The return to رضى links this promised entry to the section’s final satisfaction.
terra: The God-fearing have whatever they wish eternally in the Garden, and it is described as a promise incumbent upon the Lord and asked for.

luna: Whoever brings good receives what is better than it and is safe from terror (“فَلَهُۥ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهَا”). This links good action to a better final outcome and contrasts with the section’s denied promise. | terra: Whoever comes with a good deed receives better than it and security from that Day's terror, a nonlexical picture of the best final outcome.
terra: Whoever comes with an evil deed is cast face-first into the Fire and asked whether the requital is anything but what they did, supplying 27:89's opposite direction.
terra: Whatever people are given is temporary worldly enjoyment, while what is with Allah is better and lasting; it exposes the mistake of clutching the present gift.

terra: The one given a good promise and then meeting it is contrasted with one merely furnished with worldly enjoyment before being brought for judgment; this is the section's promised best end versus present possession almost in miniature.
terra: Praise belongs to Allah in the first life and the hereafter, judgment belongs to Him, and all return to Him; both domains and final verdict remain His.
terra: People are told to seek the home of the hereafter with what Allah has given them and to do good as He did good to them; the present gift becomes the means of the final home.
terra: Whoever brings a good deed receives better than it, while evil-doers are requited only for what they did; the ayah states both directions and a superior good return.
luna: Believers who do good are promised recompense according to “بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ.” It directly parallels the section’s al-husnā as the good end granted for faithful action.

luna: The section’s named form الآخرة is glossed as the second creation; this ayah explicitly says God brings about “ٱلنَّشْأَةَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ,” supporting that reading of the final abode. | terra: The command to survey creation leads to ثُمَّ اللَّهُ يُنْشِئُ النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ, explicitly identifying the hereafter with the section's “second creation.”
terra: Allah's promise is declared true and unfailing, establishing the reliability that the section's confirmer trusts and its denier rejects.
terra: People know only the outward aspect of worldly life while remaining heedless of the hereafter; this explains the near-sighted posture opposite trusting 30:6's promise.
terra: The end of those who did evil is السُّوأَىٰ because they denied Allah's signs; it names al-husna's stated opposite and ties that opposite end to enacted denial.

luna: This directs giving to relatives, the poor, and the traveler, and names seeking God’s face as the motive. It is another specific instance of the section’s giving for God rather than a person’s repayment. | terra: Giving the relative, poor person, and traveler is assigned to those يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ اللَّهِ, directly matching the giver who seeks only the face of his Lord.
terra: Wealth advanced to grow within people's wealth does not grow with Allah, whereas zakat given seeking His face is multiplied; it tests whether return is sought from people or from God.
terra: Those who believe and do right have Gardens of bliss, so the promised destination follows enacted faith.
terra: Their abiding Garden is وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا, explicitly naming the good end of 31:8 as God's true promise.
terra: Believers who do right receive Gardens as hospitality for what they used to do, making the good destination a requital of enacted faith.
terra: The defiantly disobedient have the Fire and are told to taste what they used to deny, the enacted denial and adverse recompense opposite 32:19.
terra: When believers see the confederates they say this is what Allah and His Messenger promised and وَصَدَقَ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ; the event increases their faith and submission rather than denial.
terra: Some believers صَدَقُوا مَا عَاهَدُوا اللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ and then fulfill or await fulfillment; endurance and sacrifice embody truth toward what was pledged.

luna: The section’s named root ص د ق includes making an expectation come true; this ayah says Iblis’s expectation was made true (“صَدَّقَ … ظَنَّهُۥ”). The root’s fulfillment sense appears here in a contrary outcome. | terra: وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ is the section's quoted secondary sense: people's following makes Iblis's supposition come true, an ominous counterpart to confirming al-husna.
terra: Iblis had no coercive authority; his realized supposition in 34:20 serves to distinguish one who believes in the hereafter from one in doubt, clarifying how followers make it true.

luna: The section’s giver releases wealth for God’s sake; here God says whatever is spent He replaces (“فَهُوَ يُخْلِفُهُۥ”). The replacement promise makes the future side of giving explicit. | terra: Allah expands and restricts provision and replaces whatever people spend; the provider Himself guarantees the giver's return.
terra: إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ is followed by a warning not to let the worldly life or the deceiver delude, the precise choice between trusting the promised end and retaining the near one.

luna: Those who spend from what God provided hope for “تِجَـٰرَةًۭ لَّن تَبُورَ,” a trade that will not fail. This gives the section’s present gift for a promised end the form of a lasting return. | terra: Those who recite, pray, and spend secretly and openly hope for a commerce that will never perish, recasting present giving as trust in an enduring return.

luna: The neighbor explains the trade in 35:29: God pays their rewards in full and increases them from His bounty (“لِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ أُجُورَهُمْ وَيَزِيدَهُم”). It completes the promised return on giving. | terra: Allah will pay those spenders their rewards in full and add from His bounty, supplying the promised repayment of 35:29's imperishable commerce.
terra: At resurrection the awakened recognize هَذَا مَا وَعَدَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ وَصَدَقَ الْمُرْسَلُونَ, so the second creation itself verifies the announced promise.
terra: Abraham's obedient action is answered with قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ الرُّؤْيَا; conduct, rather than assent alone, makes the announced vision true, just as giving confirms al-husna.
terra: The God-fearing are promised لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ, a beautiful final return that expresses the section's “best end” without the noun al-husna.
terra: The transgressors instead have لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ, the evil return that makes 38:49's beautiful end a concrete opposition.
terra: The God-fearing receive lofty Garden chambers under which rivers flow, followed by the assurance that Allah does not fail the promise.
terra: The one who lies about Allah and كَذَّبَ بِالصِّدْقِ when truth arrives embodies the section's act of assigning the promised truth to falsehood.
terra: The one who brings truth and صَدَّقَ بِهِ stands immediately opposite 39:32; the confirmers are identified as the God-fearing.

luna: Those who do good receive whatever they wish with their Lord, “ذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ.” Their desired recompense gives the section’s final satisfaction a specific form. | terra: Those confirmers have whatever they desire عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ, and the ayah calls this جَزَاءُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ, the rightful “with their Lord” counterpart to 41:50's presumption.

luna: God removes the worst of the righteous people’s deeds and rewards them according to “بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ.” This repeats the section’s better-than-deed measure for recompense. | terra: Allah removes their worst deeds and rewards them by the best of what they did, completing the confirmation scene with gracious final recompense.
luna: The God-fearing are led in groups to the Garden and welcomed through its opened gates. This begins the final-home scene that 39:74 describes as God’s fulfilled promise.

luna: The Garden’s people say God fulfilled His promise to them and gave them the land to inherit; it is called an excellent reward for workers. This directly stages the promise’s fulfillment and satisfied recipient. | terra: The Garden's inheritors say صَدَقَنَا وَعْدَهُ: Allah has made His promise true and given them the land of the Garden as their settled end.
terra: This ayah supplies 41:50's transition: the person tirelessly asks for good but despairs when harm touches him, before mercy turns into his claim of guaranteed al-husna.

luna: The section’s wording al-husnā (root ح س ن) is put in a man’s boast, “إِنَّ لِي عِندَهُۥ لَلْحُسْنَىٰ”: he presumes the best is owed to him if returned to God, reversing the giver’s trust in a promise. | terra: After relief from distress, the self-assured man claims لِي عِنْدَهُ لَلْحُسْنَىٰ even if returned to his Lord; he assumes the promised best without confirming it through giving.
terra: After the boast of 41:50, the human turns away when favored and makes lengthy prayer when harmed, exposing the self-serving posture behind his claimed entitlement.

luna: The one who seeks the harvest of the Hereafter has it increased, while the one who seeks the world’s harvest receives no share in the Hereafter. The present labor/future return and opposed aims make a specific parallel to the section. | terra: Whoever desires the harvest of the hereafter receives increase in it, while one who desires the worldly harvest receives some of it but no share in the hereafter; action now selects its end.
terra: What people are given is worldly enjoyment, while what is with Allah is better and more lasting for believers who trust their Lord.

luna: The verse describes the recompense for evil as its like, then says that whoever forgives and reconciles has reward with God. It concretely shows the section’s root ج ز ي reaching both punitive and rewarding outcomes.
terra: Creation in truth serves a result in which every soul is requited for what it earned without injustice, stating the neutral two-way scope of jazāʾ.

luna: God accepts the best of these people’s deeds, overlooks their evils, admits them among the Garden’s people, and calls it “وَعْدَ ٱلصِّدْقِ.” This tightly joins good action, the promised end, and its fulfillment. | terra: Those whose best deeds are accepted enter the Garden in fulfillment of وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ الَّذِي كَانُوا يُوعَدُونَ, an exact scene of the true promise becoming their good end.
terra: A son rejects his parents' promise of being raised, though they tell him إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ; his speech stages the denial of the promised second creation opposite 46:16.
terra: The resurrection-denier of 46:17 joins earlier doomed communities as the word becomes due against him; the disputed promise thus reaches its adverse direction.

luna: People are called to spend, some withhold, and whoever withholds does so against himself; God is self-sufficient while people are needy. This directly reverses the section’s giver and the miser who thinks himself independent. | terra: Those invited to spend include people who withhold, but whoever withholds does so against himself; Allah is the self-sufficient one, reversing the miser's imagined independence.
terra: Allah is pleased with believers at the pledge because He knows what is in their hearts, then sends tranquility and near victory; an enacted commitment meets divine رضا.
terra: لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيَا states that Allah made the Messenger's vision true in the believers' eventual secure entry, exemplifying the root's realization sense.
terra: At the Garden the righteous hear هَٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ, turning a guarded unseen promise into a present welcome.
terra: The Garden's people have whatever they wish and Allah has “more,” closely paralleling al-husna plus ziyāda in 10:26.
terra: What people are promised is declared true, directly answering the section's question whether the announced end is truth or falsehood.
terra: The recompense is certain to occur, specifying the event whose promised truth 51:5 asserts.
terra: فَلِلَّهِ الْآخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَىٰ is the near-verbatim counterpart of 92:13: the final and the first belong to Allah.

luna: The section’s root ح س ن and root ج ز ي meet here: those who do good receive al-husnā, while those who do evil are recompensed for their deeds. It makes the section’s two-sided outcome explicit. | terra: Allah owns all in the heavens and earth so that evil is requited and those who do good are requited بِالْحُسْنَىٰ; this states the section's divine measure exactly.
terra: A human being has only what he strives for, making enacted striving rather than a claimed entitlement the basis of the coming result.
terra: A person's striving will be seen, so the act that confirms or denies an expected end is itself destined for disclosure.
terra: That striving will then be requited with the fullest recompense, extending 53:31's divine measure from good and evil to each person's visible effort.
terra: وَأَنَّ عَلَيْهِ النَّشْأَةَ الْأُخْرَىٰ assigns the other creation to Allah, giving the ontological ground for the promised final recompense.
terra: هَلْ جَزَاءُ الْإِحْسَانِ إِلَّا الْإِحْسَانُ turns doing good and its beautiful recompense into a compact reciprocal rule.
terra: Knowledge of the first creation is offered as a reminder of the next, complementing the section's use of the hereafter for the second creation.
luna: Believers are told to spend from what God has made them successors over, and those who believe and spend receive a great reward. It links entrusted wealth to the section’s promised end.

luna: The verse distinguishes those who spent before victory from those who spent later, then says good is promised to all. It makes the timing of the section’s “give today” detail consequential while preserving the shared promise. | terra: After distinguishing those who spend and struggle before and after victory, Allah says وَكُلًّا وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنَىٰ; present giving stands beside the promised best end.

luna: The invitation to lend God a good loan (“يُقْرِضُ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًۭا”) promises multiplication and noble reward. It makes the section’s giving as an investment in the promised end concrete. | terra: Whoever lends Allah a good loan is promised multiplication and a noble reward, a compact statement of giving now for divine recompense.

luna: This ayah names men and women who give charity and lend God a good loan, then promises multiplication and noble reward. It extends the section’s gift-for-future-recompense relation to both charitable forms. | terra: Charitable men and women make Allah a good loan that is multiplied, and they receive a noble reward; giving now becomes the act oriented to divine repayment.
terra: The hereafter contains severe punishment, forgiveness, and رِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ, setting the two directions of final recompense against the passing play and wealth of worldly life.
terra: Those whose hearts are strengthened with faith receive Gardens before رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ; loyalty enacted in this life ends in two-way satisfaction.

luna: The emigrants leave homes and property while seeking God’s bounty and approval (“فَضْلًا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضْوَٰنًۭا”), a concrete case of giving up what one has for God rather than a person’s repayment.

luna: The Helpers prefer the emigrants over themselves even when they are in need (“وَلَوْ كَانَ بِهِمْ خَصَاصَةٌۭ”); their generosity under scarcity sharpens the section’s contrast with the self-sufficient miser.

luna: The verse tells each soul to look at what it has sent ahead for tomorrow (“مَّا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍۢ”) while fearing God. It states the section’s present act measured against the coming end. | terra: Every soul is told to look at what it has sent ahead for tomorrow, a precise nonlexical formulation of present action making the announced future its own.
luna: This asks whether people should be guided to a trade that saves them from painful punishment. The trade image frames the next ayah’s commitment and reward as a return on present action.
luna: The trade in 61:10 is belief and striving with wealth and lives. That specific costly commitment parallels the section’s giving for the promised end; 61:12 supplies the reward.
luna: The promised return for the trade in 61:10–11 is forgiveness and Gardens. It makes the afterlife reward in that transaction explicit.
terra: People are commanded to spend before death, when the one who withheld begs for delay so that he may give charity and become righteous; the unrealized gift exposes his earlier choice.
terra: Allah will not delay a soul when its term arrives, closing 63:10's regret and making the time for action irrecoverable.
terra: Wealth and children are a trial while a tremendous reward is with Allah, preparing 64:16–17's command to overcome stinginess and spend.

luna: The section sets its giver against the miser; this verse says those protected from the self’s stinginess (“شُحَّ نَفْسِهِۦ”) are the successful, directly marking generosity as the boundary. | terra: The command to spend for one's own good stands against the soul's stinginess, and those protected from it are the successful, closely restaging 92's giver and miser.

luna: The neighbor to 64:16 describes lending God a good loan and God multiplying it. It completes the successful escape from stinginess with the promised divine recompense. | terra: A good loan to Allah is multiplied and forgiven, giving 64:16's spender a promised divine return rather than a repayment from a person.
terra: The people of the Blaze admit that a warner came but they denied and declared the revelation false, showing verbal denial arriving at its warned end.

luna: The saved speaker says, “إِنِّى مُلَـٰقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ,” that he expected to meet his account. It gives a concrete instance of expectation proven in the later reckoning, as in the section’s account of ص د ق.
luna: The saved person is in “عِيشَةٍۢ رَّاضِيَةٍۢ,” a pleasing life. It gives a positive outcome of satisfaction alongside the section’s promised رضى; 69:22 identifies the Garden.
luna: The saved person’s outcome is a high Garden (“جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍۢ”), the Paradise gloss the section gives for al-husnā; it completes the pleasing life of 69:21.
luna: The saved are told to eat and drink in satisfaction for what they sent ahead in past days (“بِمَآ أَسْلَفْتُمْ”). It directly links present action to later satisfaction.

luna: The condemned person says, “مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّى مَالِيَهْ,” that his wealth did not avail him. This is the section’s withheld wealth reaching its opposite outcome; 69:29 says his authority is gone.
luna: The condemned person says his authority has perished (“هَلَكَ عَنِّى سُلْطَٰنِيَهْ”), completing 69:28’s failure of wealth to help him and reversing the giver’s assured end.
luna: The condemned person “وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰ,” gathering and hoarding wealth. This is a concrete reversal of the section’s giver, whose wealth is released for the final outcome.
terra: Whatever good people advance for themselves will be found with Allah as better and greater in reward, directly locating the return of present giving with God.
terra: The command not to confer a favor seeking increase can be read as a boundary against giving in expectation of a larger human return, the motive excluded in 92:19.
terra: People love the immediate life, naming the attachment that makes retaining the present seem preferable to confirming the promised end.
terra: They leave the hereafter behind, completing 75:20's diagnosis as an active abandonment of the final life.
terra: فَلَا صَدَّقَ وَلَا صَلَّىٰ denies the condemned person both confirmation and prayer; it is the unperformed side of the section's action-based tasdiq.
terra: وَلَٰكِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ gives the positive description of his refusal, echoing 92:16's exact denial-and-turning pair.

luna: The section’s giver parts with wealth; here the righteous feed the poor, orphan, and captive (“وَيُطْعِمُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ”). Neighbor 76:9 adds their motive of seeking God’s face without expecting payment. | terra: They give food, despite loving or needing it, to the poor, orphan, and captive; this supplies the concrete giving whose pure motive 76:9 states.

luna: The section says the giver seeks the Lord’s face and no person’s repayment; this ayah states “لِوَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ” and “لَا نُرِيدُ مِنكُمْ جَزَآءًۭ,” making that motive and refusal of human recompense explicit. | terra: The feeders say إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ and seek neither جَزَاءً nor thanks from people, the closest parallel to 92:19–20's giver without a human return.

luna: After the feeding and refusal of human payment in 76:8–9, the givers explain that they fear a grim Day from their Lord. This names the future judgment that gives their present act its direction. | terra: The feeders explain that they fear a grim Day from their Lord, identifying the promised future that governs their present gift.

luna: God protects this group from that Day and gives them radiance and joy. It completes the reward of the selfless givers in 76:8–10 and makes the section’s final satisfaction visible. | terra: Allah protects those givers from that Day's evil and grants radiance and joy, beginning the divine answer to their unrepaid act.

luna: The same group is rewarded for patience with a Garden and silk (“وَجَزَىٰهُم بِمَا صَبَرُوا۟ جَنَّةًۭ”). This supplies the Paradise meant by the section’s al-husnā. | terra: Because of their patient action Allah requites them with a Garden and silk, showing the otherworldly recompense that replaces the human payment disclaimed in 76:9.

luna: The passage closes, “إِنَّ هَـٰذَا كَانَ لَكُمْ جَزَآءًۭ وَكَانَ سَعْيُكُم مَّشْكُورًا”: the gift-givers’ effort is appreciated and rewarded, joining their act to the section’s promised satisfaction. | terra: In the Garden they are told إِنَّ هَٰذَا كَانَ لَكُمْ جَزَاءً and that their striving was appreciated, completing giving without earthly return in acknowledged final reward.
terra: Those opposed to the selfless feeders love the immediate life and leave behind a weighty day, making preference for the present the reason the promised end is neglected.
luna: This describes the one who preferred the worldly life (“وَءَاثَرَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا”), a specific counterpart to choosing present possession over the section’s better last end.
luna: The person who fears standing before his Lord and restrains the soul from desire (“خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِۦ”) fits the section’s God-fearing giver; 79:41 supplies the Garden that is his refuge.
luna: This neighbor names the God-fearing person’s refuge as the Garden, completing the contrast with 79:38 and the section’s al-husnā as Paradise.

luna: This passage begins the face contrast also stated in 10:26–27: one group has radiant faces (“مُّسْفِرَةٌۭ”), while the following verses describe the opposite group. It gives another visible form to the section’s opposed ends.
luna: The radiant group is laughing and glad (“ضَاحِكَةٌۭ مُّسْتَبْشِرَةٌۭ”); 80:40–41 then turns to dusty, darkened faces. This sharpens the section’s contrast in final outcome.
luna: The opposing group’s faces bear dust (“عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌۭ”), the reverse of 80:38–39 and of the unclouded faces in 10:26.
luna: The same opposing faces are covered by darkness (“تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌۭ”), completing the face scene that 10:26–27 uses for good and evil outcomes.
terra: At the Fire the deniers are told هَٰذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ; the promised object they denied has become the scene confronting them.

luna: The section’s ease outcome in 92:7 uses the same divine promise of being eased toward ease; here God says “وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ” to the Prophet. The shared root/formula extends the ease language to a different addressee.

luna: This ayah says people prefer the nearer life (“تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا”), a specific counterpart to the section’s concern with giving now for the afterlife. | terra: بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا identifies preferring the nearer life as the choice opposite giving what is present for the promised end.

luna: The section’s form الآخرة identifies the final abode; this ayah states that the Hereafter is better and more enduring (“خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰ”), directly supporting its value over the first life. | terra: وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ supplies the reason for reversing that preference: the final is better and more lasting.

luna: The radiant, blissful faces (“وُجُوهٌۭ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ نَّاعِمَةٌۭ”) introduce the blessed group whose effort is satisfying in 88:9 and whose Garden follows in 88:10, extending the section’s final satisfaction scene.

luna: The blessed are “لِّسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌۭ,” satisfied with their striving. This directly connects the section’s ر ض و satisfaction to the outcome of a person’s effort; 88:10 names the Garden. | terra: A joyous face in the hereafter is satisfied with its striving, linking final رضا directly to the action previously performed.

luna: The neighbor completes the pleased workers’ outcome with “فِى جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍۢ.” It makes the Garden that accompanies their satisfaction explicit. | terra: That satisfied face is in a lofty Garden, specifying the destination in which 88:9's satisfaction is completed.
terra: At judgment a person wishes he had sent something ahead for his true life, a regretful reversal of the giver who already transferred the present into the final end.

luna: The next verse 89:28 calls the soul to return pleased and pleasing; this neighboring address identifies it as “ٱلنَّفْسُ ٱلْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ,” a reassured soul, linking the section’s satisfaction to its final return. | terra: يَا أَيَّتُهَا النَّفْسُ الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ identifies the soul addressed by 89:28, making satisfaction part of a completed, tranquil return.

luna: The section names the two directions of ر ض و; this return is “رَاضِيَةًۭ مَّرْضِيَّةًۭ,” the soul pleased and pleasing, joining its satisfaction to God’s approval. | terra: The tranquil soul is told to return to its Lord رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً, holding the servant's satisfaction and the Lord's satisfaction in one return.
terra: The satisfied soul enters among God's servants before entering the Garden, one step in the return scene surrounding 89:28.
terra: The mutually satisfied soul is told to enter the Garden, naming the destination that completes the return of 89:28.

luna: The section’s root ء خ ر marks the afterlife; this neighboring surah says “وَلَلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْأُولَىٰ.” It states the better-last-than-first ordering before 93:5’s giving and satisfaction. | terra: وَلَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَكَ مِنَ الْأُولَىٰ immediately grounds 93:5's promised giving and satisfaction in the final being better than the first.

luna: The closing wording “وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ” is repeated with a changed giver: here the Lord gives the Prophet, who is satisfied. This turns the section’s human gift and promised satisfaction into a divine gift. | terra: وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ reverses the section's roles: here the Lord gives and the recipient reaches the same promised satisfaction.

luna: The disbelievers are called the worst of creation and assigned to Hell; 98:7 names the believers the best of creation and 98:8 gives their mutual satisfaction. This supplies the adverse side of that neighboring reward scene. | terra: Disbelievers abide in Hell as the worst of creatures, supplying the direct opposing fate to 98:7–8's best creatures, Garden, and mutual satisfaction.

luna: Believers who do good are called “خَيْرُ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ,” the best of creation. The next ayah gives their Garden and mutual pleasure, linking the section’s al-husnā to those who believe and act. | terra: Those who believe and do righteous deeds are called the best of creatures, identifying the agents whose Garden and mutual satisfaction 98:8 announces.

luna: The section’s root ر ض و is expressed in both directions here: “رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ.” Their garden reward culminates in God’s pleasure and theirs. | terra: Garden-reward culminates in رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ, explicitly stating both directions of satisfaction developed in the section.

luna: The section’s root ج ز ي concerns what comes back to a person; here even an atom’s weight of good is seen (“مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًۭا يَرَهُۥ”), making the final accounting tangible. | terra: Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, making even the smallest present act meet its final disclosure.

luna: The paired ayah says an atom’s weight of evil is seen too (“مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍۢ شَرًّۭا يَرَهُۥ”). It supplies the adverse side of the section’s two-way recompense. | terra: Whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it, supplying the equal adverse direction beside 99:7's good act.
